sources.title: The Macroeconomic Aggregates for England, 1209–2008
sources.author: Gregory Clark
sources.bibliographic_ref: UC Davis Economics Working Paper 09-19, revised October 2009; Tables 1, 4, 27 (PDF pp.53–56,74–75).
sources.notes: Original author working paper fetched and relevant tables extracted. Quantities retain this model vintage. Full publication not redistributed. 1200s excluded because the author says evidence represents 1209 alone; 1620s excluded because the decade extends beyond scope.

sources.title: The Sweet Track and Climate Change
sources.notes: Dendrochronological account citing Hillam et al. (1990). The measured felling window and later repairs are separate assertions.

records.name: English nominal farm wages, Clark 2009
records.methodology: Table 1 decadal model means, including estimated harvest premium; not real wages or individual observed earnings. Accounting-year allocation follows the author’s convention.

records.name: English cost-of-living index, Clark 2009
records.methodology: Table 27 cost-of-living column; weighted historical price reconstruction. The reference period is outside the dataset scope but no observations after 1625 are imported.

records.notes: This rounded scope-opening anchor does not imply simultaneous adoption everywhere.

records.description: Timbers felled in winter 3807/3806 BCE or early spring 3806 BCE.
records.notes: Felling is the dendrochronologically measured event; construction closely associated but not an invented exact day.
